name: Implement a Task
description: Plan → you approve → implement → test → review. Works from a ticket key, a link or a plain description; no Jira setup needed. Leaves the change uncommitted for you.

config.prompt: Read the repository instructions first. Plan this task: {{input.task}}. If it is a ticket key or link you can open, read it first. List the files to change, the tests to add and the risks. Do not edit any files.

config.message: Check the plan before any file changes.

config.prompt: Read the repository instructions first. Implement the approved plan for: {{input.task}}. Keep the change focused and add or update tests. Do not run the test suite or commit; the workflow does both.

Read the repository instructions first. Review the uncommitted changes in this repository (run `git diff`) for this task: {{input.task}}. Report each problem as a ```finding block with the lines `severity:` (P0 for data loss, security holes or crashes; P1 for wrong behavior or missing tests for changed logic; P2 or P3 for minor issues), `file:`, `line:`, `title:`, `explanation:` and `fix:`. If there is nothing to report, say so in one sentence without severity labels.

inputs.name: task
inputs.label: Task: ticket key, link or description

inputs.name: testCommand
inputs.label: Test command (e.g. npm test, cargo test, make test)

name: Review Pull Request
description: Load a PR and its diff → Claude and Codex review in parallel → if they find P0/P1 problems, you approve posting one comment; otherwise it is marked clean.

config.prompt: Read the repository instructions first. Review pull request #{{input.prNumber}} using its details and diff above. Open files in this repository for context when the diff is not enough. Report each problem as a ```finding block with the lines `severity:` (P0 for data loss, security holes or crashes; P1 for wrong behavior or missing tests for changed logic; P2 or P3 for minor issues), `file:`, `line:`, `title:`, `explanation:` and `fix:`. If there is nothing to report, say so in one sentence without severity labels.

Read the repository instructions first. Deep review of pull request #{{input.prNumber}} (details and diff above): correctness, security and missing tests. Report each problem as a ```finding block with the lines `severity:` (P0 for data loss, security holes or crashes; P1 for wrong behavior or missing tests for changed logic; P2 or P3 for minor issues), `file:`, `line:`, `title:`, `explanation:` and `fix:`. If there is nothing to report, say so in one sentence without severity labels.

config.message: The reviews found P0/P1 problems. Approve to post them as one comment on the PR; reject to stop without posting.

args: No P0/P1 findings in pull request {{input.prNumber}}.

inputs.name: prNumber
inputs.label: Pull request number (e.g. 128)

name: Investigate Bug
description: Find the root cause and add a failing regression test → you confirm → fix → test. Leaves the change uncommitted for you.

config.prompt: Read the repository instructions first. Investigate this bug: {{input.bug}}. Find the root cause and add a regression test that fails because of it, but do not fix the bug yet. Explain the cause and name the new test. Do not run the test suite or commit; the workflow does both.

config.message: Check the explanation and the new regression test before the fix.

config.prompt: Read the repository instructions first. Fix the root cause described above. Keep the new regression test and do not weaken existing tests. Do not run the test suite or commit; the workflow does both.

inputs.name: bug
inputs.label: Bug: issue key, link or description

inputs.name: testCommand
inputs.label: Test command (e.g. npm test, cargo test, make test)

name: Refactor
description: Run the tests → refactor without changing behavior → run the tests again → review. Leaves the change uncommitted for you.

config.prompt: Read the repository instructions first. Refactor without changing behavior: {{input.target}}. Keep public interfaces and existing tests unchanged. Do not run the test suite or commit; the workflow does both.

Read the repository instructions first. Review the uncommitted refactor (run `git diff`) for any change in behavior. The goal was: {{input.target}}. Report each problem as a ```finding block with the lines `severity:` (P0 for data loss, security holes or crashes; P1 for wrong behavior or missing tests for changed logic; P2 or P3 for minor issues), `file:`, `line:`, `title:`, `explanation:` and `fix:`. If there is nothing to report, say so in one sentence without severity labels.

inputs.name: target
inputs.label: What to refactor and the goal (e.g. split src/cart.ts into smaller modules)

inputs.name: testCommand
inputs.label: Test command (e.g. npm test, cargo test, make test)

name: Dependency Upgrade
description: Update the manifest and adapt the code → install → test → review the upgrade. Leaves the change uncommitted for you.

config.prompt: Read the repository instructions first. Upgrade {{input.dependency}}: change the version in the dependency manifest and adapt the code to its breaking changes. Do not run the package manager; the workflow installs next. Do not run the test suite or commit; the workflow does both.

Read the repository instructions first. Review the upgrade of {{input.dependency}} (run `git diff`) for breaking changes and risky API use. Report each problem as a ```finding block with the lines `severity:` (P0 for data loss, security holes or crashes; P1 for wrong behavior or missing tests for changed logic; P2 or P3 for minor issues), `file:`, `line:`, `title:`, `explanation:` and `fix:`. If there is nothing to report, say so in one sentence without severity labels.

inputs.name: dependency
inputs.label: Dependency and target version (e.g. react to 19.3)

inputs.name: installCommand
inputs.label: Install command that updates the lockfile (e.g. pnpm install, npm install, cargo update)

inputs.name: testCommand
inputs.label: Test command (e.g. npm test, cargo test, make test)

name: Run Multi-Agent Review
description: Diff this branch and your uncommitted work against a base branch → Claude and Codex review in parallel → triage P0/P1 findings or mark it clean.

config.prompt: Read the repository instructions first. Review the changes in the diff above (this branch and uncommitted work compared with {{input.base}}). Open files in this repository for context when the diff is not enough. Report each problem as a ```finding block with the lines `severity:` (P0 for data loss, security holes or crashes; P1 for wrong behavior or missing tests for changed logic; P2 or P3 for minor issues), `file:`, `line:`, `title:`, `explanation:` and `fix:`. If there is nothing to report, say so in one sentence without severity labels.

Read the repository instructions first. Deep review of the diff above (compared with {{input.base}}): correctness, security and missing tests. Report each problem as a ```finding block with the lines `severity:` (P0 for data loss, security holes or crashes; P1 for wrong behavior or missing tests for changed logic; P2 or P3 for minor issues), `file:`, `line:`, `title:`, `explanation:` and `fix:`. If there is nothing to report, say so in one sentence without severity labels.

config.message: The reviews found P0/P1 problems. Read them in Runs, then approve to finish.

inputs.name: base
inputs.label: Compare against branch

name: Create Draft PR
description: Check out your branch → test → review → you approve → push and open a draft PR.

config.prompt: Read the repository instructions first. Review the commits on this branch compared with {{input.base}} (run `git diff {{input.base}}...HEAD`). Report each problem as a ```finding block with the lines `severity:` (P0 for data loss, security holes or crashes; P1 for wrong behavior or missing tests for changed logic; P2 or P3 for minor issues), `file:`, `line:`, `title:`, `explanation:` and `fix:`. If there is nothing to report, say so in one sentence without severity labels.

config.message: Check the review. Approving pushes the branch and opens a draft pull request.

name: Address Review Feedback
description: Check out a PR → address its review feedback → test → re-review, with up to two fix rounds. A feedback watcher can run it with the PR number. Leaves the change uncommitted for you.

config.prompt: Read the repository instructions first. Address the review feedback on pull request #{{input.prNumber}} shown above. Change only what the feedback asks for and add tests where needed. Do not run the test suite or commit; the workflow does both.

Read the repository instructions first. Review the uncommitted changes (run `git diff`) against the PR feedback above. Report each problem as a ```finding block with the lines `severity:` (P0 for data loss, security holes or crashes; P1 for wrong behavior or missing tests for changed logic; P2 or P3 for minor issues), `file:`, `line:`, `title:`, `explanation:` and `fix:`. If there is nothing to report, say so in one sentence without severity labels.
Read the repository instructions first. Fix the P0/P1 findings from the review above. Do not run the test suite or commit; the workflow does both.

inputs.name: prNumber
inputs.label: Pull request number (e.g. 128)

inputs.name: testCommand
inputs.label: Test command (e.g. npm test, cargo test, make test)

name: Ticket to Draft PR
description: Jira ticket → branch → implement → test → Claude and Codex review → fix loop → you review → commit, push and open a draft PR. Needs a Jira MCP server.

config.prompt: Read the repository instructions first. Implement {{ticket.key}}: {{ticket.title}} using the ticket details above. Keep the change focused and add or update tests. Do not run the test suite or commit; the workflow does both.

Read the repository instructions first. Review the uncommitted changes for {{ticket.key}} (run `git diff`) against the ticket above. Report each problem as a ```finding block with the lines `severity:` (P0 for data loss, security holes or crashes; P1 for wrong behavior or missing tests for changed logic; P2 or P3 for minor issues), `file:`, `line:`, `title:`, `explanation:` and `fix:`. If there is nothing to report, say so in one sentence without severity labels.

Read the repository instructions first. Deep review of the uncommitted changes for {{ticket.key}} (run `git diff`): correctness, security and missing tests. Report each problem as a ```finding block with the lines `severity:` (P0 for data loss, security holes or crashes; P1 for wrong behavior or missing tests for changed logic; P2 or P3 for minor issues), `file:`, `line:`, `title:`, `explanation:` and `fix:`. If there is nothing to report, say so in one sentence without severity labels.
Read the repository instructions first. Fix the P0/P1 findings from both reviews above. Do not run the test suite or commit; the workflow does both.

config.message: Check the change and the review findings. Approving commits the change, pushes the branch and opens a draft pull request.
